subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Every-PR mutmut can never fail on a surviving mutant: pinned tool has no score-failure semantics, scope is 1.9% of the tree
evidence: .github/workflows/mutation-testing.yml:38 (uv run mutmut run, no threshold, no continue-on-error) + mutmut-3.8.0 mutmut/__main__.py run()->None (nonzero exit only at :334/:865/:995 harness errors; no fail-under flag) + pyproject.toml:328-332 (source_paths = async_helpers 1,363 + lsp 1,975 + response_processing.py 860 = 4,198 LOC of 218,066 non-test backend LOC) and pyproject.toml:341-355 (test selection 15 files)
one_why: The provisional verification-9 anchor reads as enforcement but is telemetry: a green step-summary table is the only output a surviving mutant produces, and even a fixed gate would cover ~2% of the tree - the study's first mutation-testing claim enters the corpus as its cautionary tale (ledger rule: cite the line that blocks; none exists here).

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: LLM-eval PR workflow is a dead skeleton: asset-detect step finds its own required files missing, so every PR lands on the skip-explainer job
evidence: .github/workflows/integration-runner.yml:31-44 (detect requires backend/evaluation/agent_eval_pack.py and evaluation/integration_tests/scripts/run_infer.sh) vs ls evaluation/ = __init__.py + deepswe only; :57-64 runs 'Integration workflow skipped (assets missing)' whenever available != true - the permanent state; same shape self-declared at .github/workflows/vscode-extension-build.yml:4
one_why: On paper the repo shows a per-PR Haiku+DeepSeek eval job (run_infer.sh llm.eval - openhands idiom), which is exactly the kind of workflow-file evidence the protocol credits; the nuance reviewers must learn: always check the gating asset exists in-tree, or CI breadth becomes fiction - convergence candidate with test-suite-without-ci (sibling axis: workflow-without-work).

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Security-analyzer exception falls the effective risk DOWN to the model's own declared level, LOW when undeclared
evidence: backend/execution/aes/security_enforcement.py:526-541 (except Exception -> analyzer_risk=None; declared UNKNOWN -> LOW) vs :543-551 (analyzer can only escalate when it succeeds)
one_why: The classifier normally ratchets upward, but any analyzer crash converts an unclassified shell command into model-self-certified LOW - the exact inverse of deepagents' classifier-unavailable -> require_human fail-closed (auto_mode.py:3542-3546); joins the fail-open family watch (gptme confirm fail-open, nanocoder jail fail-open) as the classifier-exception variant.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Codex provider rides the user's ChatGPT subscription OAuth from a third-party loop via chatgpt.com/backend-api - ruled ToS/license class, not safety-hole
evidence: backend/inference/clients/codex_app_server.py:1-6 (module docstring: managed OAuth + direct Responses endpoint, Grinta owns loop/approvals) and :34 (_CODEX_RESPONSES_BASE_URL = https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex)
one_why: Boundary taxonomy ruling: no protection mechanism inside Grinta is advertised-but-inert (so not safety-hole); the exposure is the TERMS of credential use - subscription auth licensed for first-party Codex surfaces, account-action risk lands on the end user - which is the same usage-terms bin as kode-cli's Apache self-grant and manifest-only licenses; stays distinct from claurst-2 oauth-client-impersonation (active client/TLS spoofing) because Grinta declares its posture openly and does not evade gates; concepts-only portables.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: sandboxed_local profile hard-fails when the OS jail binary is missing (all three platforms incl. a Windows AppContainer path) and offers whole-FS immutability instead of command classification
evidence: backend/execution/sandboxing.py:205-213,222-224 (RuntimeError when bwrap/sandbox-exec absent, no silent fallback); sandboxing.py:4-6 (bubblewrap / sandbox-exec / AppContainer); backend/core/config/security_config.py:71-81 (readonly_workspace mounts the workspace read-only 'rather than classifying shell commands as read or write (unreliable...)')
one_why: The two decisions most harnesses get wrong in one config: no fail-open when the jail is unavailable (vs nanocoder's plain-sh fallback), and encoding read-only delegation as filesystem immutability rather than another regex ladder; still opt-in (execution_profile='standard' default) and interactive terminals bypass isolation by design - honest at sandboxing.py:7-10 - which keeps the subject's safety at 7, not 8.
